title: Security: Multiple Information Disclosure issues in Streamlit internal endpoints (_stcore) affecting Enterprise DAST scans
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Our application recently underwent an Enterprise DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) review.

The scanner reported multiple Information Disclosure findings originating from Streamlit internal endpoints and Tornado responses rather than application code.

The application itself already handles exceptions and returns generic messages.

The remaining findings appear to originate from Streamlit framework internals.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Enterprise deployments should have configuration options to:

• Hide Tornado Server header

• Hide Streamlit version

• Disable /_stcore/host-config endpoint

• Validate WebSocket Origin

• Return generic websocket errors

• Remove filesystem paths

• Remove OS version disclosure

These options are commonly required during DAST / Penetration Testing.

### Current Behavior

### 1. Server Banner Disclosure

HTTP Response contains

Server: TornadoServer/6.x.x

Expected:

Ability to suppress or remove the Server header.

------------------------------------------------

### 2. WebSocket Error Messages

Malformed websocket messages return internal traceback information including

browser_websocket_handler.py

filesystem paths

line numbers

Expected:

Return generic websocket error.

------------------------------------------------

### 3. Linux Version Disclosure

WebSocket responses disclose Linux version / platform details.

Expected:

No operating system information returned to clients.

------------------------------------------------

### 4. Host Configuration Disclosure

Endpoint

/_stcore/host-config

returns

allowedOrigins

including wildcard entries.

Expected:

Configuration to disable endpoint or suppress origin disclosure.

------------------------------------------------

### 5. Missing Origin Validation

Changing the Origin header during websocket upgrade still establishes the connection.

Expected:

Ability to configure allowed websocket origins.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

## Environment
Streamlit Version: 1.48.1

Python: 3.12

Deployment:

Azure App Service (Linux)

Azure Application Gateway WAF v2

OKTA OIDC Authentication

Browser:

Chrome

Enterprise Banking Application

### Additional Information

These findings were identified during Enterprise Banking security assessment.

Application code is already updated to:

• Return generic application errors

• Log detailed exceptions server-side

Remaining disclosures originate from Streamlit internal implementation.

Is there any supported configuration or roadmap to address these?

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16386)

Enterprise DAST findings about information disclosure from Streamlit internals (`/_stcore/*`, WebSocket errors, server banner), filed against **1.48.1** (Tornado). Most asks are for hardening/config options rather than broken app behavior. Likely sources: Tornado/`Server` header; WebSocket exception paths that can leak paths; `NewSession.environment_info` intentionally sending `server_os` / versions; `/_stcore/host-config` exposing `client.allowedOrigins` (needed for iframe embedding; docs already suggest proxy override for untrusted hosts); WebSocket Origin checks that are weaker when `server.enableCORS=false` or on older Tornado builds. Current Starlette/Uvicorn server adds `server.allowedHosts` and middleware for custom headers (see #9160), so several items may already be mitigable via upgrade + reverse proxy / ASGI middleware.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9160 — Closest overlap: Tornado `Server` banner disclosure and configurable HTTP security headers; closed with Starlette middleware guidance.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6417 — Earlier request for native security-header support in enterprise/cloud deployments (also closed pointing to Starlette).
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13732 — Related `/_stcore/host-config` surface; asks to extend that endpoint rather than hide it.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.5-high`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Thanks for the report. The report is for **1.48.1**. The current release is **1.61.1**. We removed Tornado in **1.57.0**. Because of that, item 1 is not correct for current releases. Most of the other items still need work.

Item by item.

**Item 2, WebSocket error messages. Confirmed bug.**

Malformed protobuf frames bypass the app-error redaction path. Because of this, `client.showErrorDetails` does not apply. File paths and line numbers can leak. This is a bug.

`client.showErrorDetails = "none"` still helps for application exceptions. It does not cover this path.

**Item 5, WebSocket Origin validation. Partly valid.**

`server.allowedHosts` was added in **1.61.0**. It validates the `Host` header on the WebSocket handshake. It still works when CORS is disabled. This helps with unexpected hostnames. It does not provide a strict `Origin` allow-list.

`server.corsAllowedOrigins` only adds more allowed origins. It does not replace the built-in allowed set. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, and the server's internal and external IPs are still allowed. `server.enableCORS=false` also allows all origins. This needs a separate feature request.

**Item 3, OS version disclosure. Partly overstated.**

Streamlit does not send a kernel version or distro version here. The `server_os` field is only `platform.system().lower()`. On Linux, this value is `"linux"`.

The same session message still exposes the full Streamlit version and full Python version to any client that can open the WebSocket. The Streamlit version is used for client auto-reload after a server upgrade. The Python version and OS name are used only for telemetry in the current frontend.

**Item 1, `Server` header. Resolved as written, but still present.**

On current releases, the header is `Server: uvicorn`. It is not `TornadoServer/6.x.x`. It does not include a version. Streamlit does not have a config option to remove it. The current workaround is to strip it at the proxy.

**Item 4, `/_stcore/host-config`. Informational.**

This endpoint returns mostly hardcoded open-source defaults and your configured `client.allowedOrigins`. It does not reveal deployment-specific secrets. For a non-embedded app, `client.allowedOrigins = []` is the correct setting.

Do not block this endpoint on the default connection path. If you need to control it, override the response at the proxy and return valid JSON.

**Next steps**

We filed two issues:

1. [WebSocket protocol error path ignores `client.showErrorDetails` and leaks stack traces](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16391)
2. [`server.enableCORS=false` warning incorrectly says the value is overridden to true](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16390)

Please split the other asks into separate issues:

1. Suppress the `Server` header
2. Add a strict WebSocket Origin allow-list
3. Suppress version and OS fields in the session message

Thankyou so much for addressing the raised issues and creating the 2 sub-issues. As guided, the item 1 is fixed using the Streamlit version 1.60.0 and remaining 2 issues have been raised. Here are the links:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16448
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16449

Could you please let me know generally, how much is the required for resolution of the already raised issues? If the issues are not fixed within next week, what could the feasible workaround so that DAST testing can be completed withing time?

Thanks for opening the separate enhancement requests. #16448 and #16449 now track those two asks.

**Status of the two bugs**

- #16391, the WebSocket protocol error path that leaked stack traces. Fixed and merged in #16392.
- #16390, the incorrect server.enableCORS=false startup warning. Fixed and merged in #16393.

Both fixes are on develop. The latest release is 1.61.1, so neither fix is released yet. We plan to release 1.62.0 within the next few weeks, and it will include both fixes.

**Status of the two enhancement requests**

We cannot give a timeline for #16448 or #16449. For your DAST timeline, please note that the remaining items are hardening and configuration requests, not confirmed vulnerabilities. 

**Closing this issue**

Every work item from this report now has its own issue. I am closing this one. Please follow the individual issues:

- #16391 (fixed, ships in 1.62.0)
- #16390 (fixed, ships in 1.62.0)
- #16448 (open)
- #16449 (open)
